findings.issue: FR-THIRDREVIEW-001 simultaneously defines 3rd-review as a zero-stage/zero-round single-call engine and keeps `--checkpoint=<stage>` on the same runner entry for standalone use. That leaves the canonical contract ambiguous: either the entrypoint still accepts stage routing, or it has been fully stripped of stage knowledge. As written, AC5-1/AC5-3/AC-D1 cannot be verified consistently.
findings.recommendation: Freeze one canonical runner contract. If 3rd-review must be stage-agnostic, remove `--checkpoint` from the runner entry entirely and move any standalone routing/debug behavior to a separate wrapper or separate debug-only script.

findings.issue: FR-WHREVIEW-003 requires heterologous rounds and same-source rounds to be counted independently, but the persisted state model later only defines a single `round_number`. After mode switching, the implementation cannot prove or replay whether it is on heterologous round 3, same-source round 2, or total round 5, so the stop/escalate rules are not machine-auditable.
findings.recommendation: Extend the round-state contract to store separate counters such as `heterologous_round`, `same_source_round`, and `total_round`, then update AC3-1/AC-D10 to validate those fields explicitly.

findings.issue: FR-D2-001 requires make-decision/build-plan/verify-code to stop at a human confirmation gate on `pass`, but no machine-consumable state or resume contract distinguishes `pass but waiting for approval` from `pass and auto-advance`. With only the three verdict enums, an orchestrator restart cannot deterministically decide whether to pause or continue.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit persisted confirmation state, such as `post_review_action=await_human_confirmation|auto_advance`, and define the artifact/command used to resume after human approval so AC8 can be implemented and tested.

resolutionSummary: 规格主方向清楚，但还有 3 个会直接卡实现和验收的契约缺口：3rd-review 入口定义前后冲突、轮次状态模型不足、人工确认门缺少可恢复状态。先补齐这三处，再进入实现。

findings.description: Spec describes a schema/contract/gate (cluster A) with soft-fail, optional, or warning-only validation — or a check that bypasses its own control switch (cluster B: soft-fail/swallow/bypass-flag terms). A gate that does not hard-block on failure allows output drift — schema-drift blocking.

Spec describes or requires eliminating internal contradictions between field contracts or rule statements (cluster A: schema/contract terms + cluster B: conflict/contradiction/duplicate terms). Multiple conflicting schemas for the same entity cause silent drift — schema-drift blocking.
